experiment: Single-person same-session EEG object recognition with support-defined hard-negative pairs.
inputs: 17 posterior EEG channels, 1003 fixed R4 features, 8 labeled calibration photos per candidate. No image, other participant, or query label as predictor. A four-word menu is provided as extra information in new_three4.
split: Replay the previous episodic object split and RNG exactly. Hold the same 96 of 512 generic objects out of all fitting, four object-disjoint OOF folds inside the remaining 416. Fit the registered native and session-centered 96-D Fisher bases out of fold. Repeat OOF training on all 512 for the two previously studied target panels. All target objects are excluded.
episodes: Separate 4- and 12-candidate menus from exactly the same session pair; independently shuffled 8 support / 2 query photo folds. For each candidate take its two nearest OTHER candidate centroids by native Fisher unit-vector cosine from permitted supports alone; ties by candidate menu order.
pair_features: For the two 96-D bases and each of their three contiguous 32-coordinate bands, whiten the difference of two candidate means by their pooled diagonal support variance shrunk halfway to its band-average variance. Project the focal EEG and both sets of 8 supports onto that discriminating direction. Fit a signed midpoint margin in units of pooled projected within-class noise, and an unequal-variance Gaussian log likelihood ratio with each class variance shrunk halfway to their pooled projected noise. Fixed support mean estimation inflation 9/8. Clip both signed contrasts to [-4,+4].
fitting: True candidate versus its two closest support-defined rivals at each object-disjoint OOF episode. Fit one intercept-free logistic residual on the 12 pair features at fixed native Fisher standardized cosine logit-difference offset. Average the two menu-size losses equally, ridge 0.1/2 squared coefficient norm. Sham flips training pair orientation labels by fair coin per two-query focal episode with same targets/supports and optimizer. No tuning.
test: Start with the earlier 16-score episodic classifier, standardized per query over the permitted menu. For each candidate add 0.5 times the average learned pair residual against its two nearest allowed support-centroid competitors. Each query is decoded independently. Wrong EEG in target uses the previous row derangement within recipient fold/menu; generic uses the two held-out peer EEGs from the next cyclic candidate in this same menu. All correct and wrong queries see exactly the same candidate supports.
checks: Reproduce all original per-row Fisher and episodic choices in both generic menus as well as stress12 and new_three4 for each participant. Use the public ordinal menu mapping for target inference before reading truth, with 12 or 4 allowed words.
endpoints: Exact top-1 object label, participant-specific hits, paired differences vs native, previous episodic, orientation-sham and wrong-EEG controls. Keep the three people fixed and resample shared object IDs (10000 percentile bootstrap, seed 260551); synchronize both generic menu sizes for each of the same 96 classes; resample 12 objects independently per target panel. Target panels and generic split are previously studied, not a new untouched dataset.
gate: Advance only if generic combined paired lower 95% bounds vs native Fisher, old episodic and orientation-sham are all strictly positive, with no menu declining vs old episodic; AND both target panels nonnegative vs old episodic, with pooled target lower bounds vs native and old episodic strictly positive. Otherwise stop. No new panel or generation.
